questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements are true with regards to a keloid scar?
options: The extent does not cross the wound margins
Wide excision of the keloid scar prevents recurrence
Histopathology of a keloid scar shows reduced collagen and increased vascularity
A keloid scar forms due to increase in the level of growth factors
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. A keloid scar forms due to increase in the level of growth factors

Keloid scars are associated with elevated levels of growth factor leading to increased proliferation of fibrous tissue.

A keloid scar is defined as excessive scar tissue that extends beyond the boundaries of the original incision or wound (option A) and rarely regresses on its own.  It is more common in darker-pigmented ethnicities.

It can arise from surgery, burns, skin inflammation, infections, ear piercing, and even spontaneously. It occurs 3 months to years after the initial insult with even minor injuries causing keloid formation.

It most commonly occurs on the skin of the earlobe, deltoid, presternal, upper back, and rarely extends into the subcutaneous tissue.

The histology of keloid scars shows excess collagen and hypervascularity with collagen fibres arranged haphazardly in loose sheets (option C).

Treatment: Keloid scars do not improve spontaneously with time and excision alone has a high rate of recurrence (option B). The following can be done:

• Pressure - local moulds or elastic garments.
• Silicone gel sheeting.
• Intralesional triamcinolone injection.
• Excision and steroid injections.
• Excision and postoperative radiation (external beam or brachytherapy).
• Intralesional excision.
• Laser to reduce redness.
• Vitamin E and palm oil massage.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: An elderly male patient presented with purulent discharge from an opening located in the perianal region. The patient is put in a lithotomy position and the opening is located at the 11 o'clock position, 4 cm from the anal margin. What will be the likely position of the internal opening and where does the internal opening start?
options: 12 o'clock and at external anal spinchter
11 o'clock and at internal anal spinchter
6 o'clock and crypt of the dentate line
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. 6 o'clock and crypt of the dentate line

The likely location of the internal opening is at 6'O clock position which is the posterior midline of the anal canal and the opening starts at the crypt of the dentate line.

The given clinical scenario is suggestive of fistula-in-ano with the external opening located at 11’O clock position, 4 cm from the anal margin. This means that the anal margin is located anterior to the coronal midsection. The location of the internal opening of the fistula can be identified based on Goodsall's rule.

Goodsall’s rule:

* Fistulas with an external opening anteriorly connect to the internal opening by a short, radial tract.

* Fistulas with an external opening posteriorly tract in a curvilinear fashion to the posterior midline.

However, exceptions to this rule often occur. Fistulas with an anterior external opening greater than 3 cm from the anal margin usually track to the posterior midline.

Thus, according to the exception to Goodsall's rule, this patient likely has an internal opening at the 6'O clock position as the external opening is located more than 3 cm from the anal margin track.

A fistula-in-ano is a chronic abnormal hollow tract or cavity that is lined with granulation tissue. It has a primary internal opening in the anorectal lumen and a secondary external opening in the perianal skin. An anal fistula may also be present if the patient has Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, malignancy, foreign body, lymphogranuloma venereum, or actinomycosis. Patients usually present with intermittent discharge and pain.

Intersphincteric fistulas are the most common type. Other types of anal fistulae are transphincteric fistula, suprasphincteric fistula, and extrasphincteric fistula.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.text:
Which of the following rules of law are associated with insanity?

1. Durham's rule
2. Curren's rule
3. Ashley's rule
4. Murphy's rule
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 only

Durham's rule and Curren's rule are laws associated with insanity.

Durhams's rule states that an accused person is not criminally responsible if his unlawful act is the product of mental disease or mental defect.

Curren’s rule states that an accused person is not criminally responsible if, at the time of committing the act, he did not have the capacity to regulate his conduct to the requirements of the law as a result of mental disease or defect.

In India, the law of Criminal responsibility is under BNS Section 22 (Section 84 IPC) It states that "Nothing is an offense which is done by a person who, at the time of doing it, by reason of unsoundness of mind, is incapable of knowing the nature of the act, or what he is doing is either wrong or contrary to the law”. This is slightly different from McNaghten's rule followed in Britain.

M'Naghten's rule states that every man is to be presumed to be sane, and possesses a sufficient degree of reason to be responsible for his crimes until the contrary is proved.

Other rules to assess the criminal responsibility of insane persons:

• The Irresistible Impulse
• Federal rule or American Law Institute test (ALT)
• The Brawner rule

Note: Ashley's rule is used to differentiate males and females based on the combined length of the manubrium and sternum. It is considered to be a male sternum when the combined length is >149 mm, while if the combined length is <149 mm, then it is considered female.
questions.learning: 1, 2 only Durham's rule and Curren's rule are laws associated with insanity. Durhams's rule states that an accused person is not criminally responsible if his unlawful act is the product of mental disease or mental defect.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.text: An elderly male who is a known smoker presented with chronic cough, significant weight loss, and fatigue. Serum calcium level is raised. A lung biopsy was done, and it showed large atypical cells with hyperchromasia. What is the probable diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Squamous cell carcinoma

The most probable diagnosis based on the given clinical scenario is squamous cell carcinoma of the lung.

Squamous cell carcinoma is most commonly found in men and is strongly associated with smoking. It predominantly arises in the central or hilar region. Histologically, it is characterized by the presence of keratin pearls and intercellular bridges.

Hypercalcemia is one of the most common paraneoplastic syndromes associated with squamous cell cancer (SCC) of the lung. Increased levels of parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTH-rP) are the most likely mechanism of his hypercalcemia. The symptoms could include anorexia, nausea, vomiting, constipation, lethargy, polyuria, polydipsia, and dehydration.

The image given below shows keratin pearls seen in squamous cell carcinomas.

Other options:

Option A: Large cell neuroendocrine tumor - These tumors are a subtype of large cell carcinoma and show neuroendocrine features on immunohistochemistry. They are aggressive and can be associated with paraneoplastic syndromes, but they do not commonly cause hypercalcemia.

Option B: Small cell carcinoma - This is a highly aggressive neuroendocrine tumor strongly associated with smoking. It frequently presents with paraneoplastic syndromes, including SIADH and ectopic ACTH production, but hypercalcemia is less common. Histologically, it is characterized by small cells with scant cytoplasm, ill-defined cell borders, and finely granular nuclear chromatin.

Option C: Adenocarcinoma - This is the most common type of lung cancer and is more common in non-smokers and women. It usually arises in the peripheral lung tissue and is associated with glandular differentiation or mucin production. Histologically, adenocarcinoma is characterized by glandular or acinar structures and/or intracytoplasmic mucin.
questions.learning: Squamous cell carcinoma — The most probable diagnosis based on the given clinical scenario is squamous cell carcinoma of the lung. Squamous cell carcinoma is most commonly found in men and is strongly associated with smoking.

Correct answer: D. A – Eccrine sweat gland, B – Arrector pilorum, C – Sebaceous gland, D – Apocrine sweat gland

Eccrine glands are small, coiled tubular glands opening directly onto the skin surface, while apocrine glands are larger, open into hair follicles, and are active after puberty.

The sebaceous gland is a lobulated holocrine gland associated with hair follicles, and the arrector pilorum is smooth muscle attaching the follicle to the dermis, responsible for piloerection.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: Which of the following is not included in the active management of the third stage of labor to prevent postpartum hemorrhage?
options: Delayed clamping, cutting and ligation of cord
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Gentle massage of uterus

As per the latest guidelines, uterine massage is no longer a core component of Active Management of the Third Stage of Labor (AMTSL) that is performed for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH).

Uterine massage or fundal massage is not recommended as an intervention to prevent PPH in women who have already received prophylactic uterotonics such as oxytocin (core component of AMTSL). Hence, it is now an optional component of AMTSL that is done in patients with uterine atony as a part of the management of PPH.

AMTSL is recommended by the WHO to prevent postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). Uterotonics are the most important components in AMTSL to do so.

The currently recommended components of AMTSL are as follows:

1.
Injecting uterotonics within 1 minute of delivery of the baby or immediately after delivery of the anterior shoulder

• Most important step
• Oxytocin 10 IU im/iv infusion is the preferred uterotonic.

(Not recommended by WHO- carboprost)

2
Delayed cord clamping

• Done within 1-3 mins of delivery
• 80 ml of additional blood goes to the fetus
• Prevents fetal anemia

3
Delivery of placenta by controlled cord traction: Modified Brandt Andrews technique

• The uterus is pushed upwards and backward
• The traction of cord is downwards and forwards

4
Intermittent assessment of uterine tone
Done every 15 mins for 2 hours

Note: In the event that uterine atony is diagnosed during the assessment of uterine tone, uterine massage can be performed to control PPH.
questions.learning: Gentle massage of uterus As per the latest guidelines, uterine massage is no longer a core component of Active Management of the Third Stage of Labor (AMTSL) that is performed for the prevention of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH).

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: In a normally distributed dataset with a mean of 82 and a standard deviation of 1.5, what is the range covered by two standard deviations from the mean?
questions.explanation: In a normal distribution, approximately 95.4% of the data falls within two standard deviations (±2 SD) of the mean. To find this range, you must calculate both the upper and lower limits from the mean value provided. Lower Limit = Mean − (2 × SD) = 82 − (2 × 1.5) = 82 − 3 = 79. Upper Limit = Mean + (2 × SD) = 82 + (2 × 1.5) = 82 + 3 = 85. Therefore, the range representing two standard deviations is 79–85. Option B, C, and D are numerically incorrect and do not follow the standard deviation formula for this data set. This statistical principle is fundamental in epidemiology and public health for determining normal reference ranges for clinical data

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: An patient presented with bleeding gums and examination findings are as below. This given condition can be seen in deficiency of _________
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Vitamin C

The given image shows perifollicular purpura. This along with corkscrew like body hair and bleeding gums is characteristic of  Scurvy (vitamin C deficiency).

* Vitamin C is a water‐soluble vitamin, antioxidant and essential co‐factor for collagen biosynthesis, carnitine, and catecholamine metabolism, and dietary iron absorption.

* Humans are unable to synthesize vitamin C; therefore, vitamin C is strictly obtained through the dietary intake of fruit and vegetables.

* Scurvy develops 1–3 months after initiating a vitamin C deficient diet.

* The cutaneous manifestations of scurvy include phrynoderma, corkscrew hairs, perifollicular hemorrhage and purpura, edema of the lower extremities, and splinter hemorrhages.

* Corkscrew hairs represent fractured and coiled hairs due to impaired keratin cross‐links by disulfide bonds. With time, significant vascular congestion occurs, particularly in the lower extremities, leading to perifollicular hemorrhage and edema.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text:
Match the following

a. Patch test
1. Leprosy

b. KOH mount
2. Lupus vulgaris

c. Biopsy
3. Contact dermatitis

d. Slit skin smear
4. Tinea corporis
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1

The correctly matched option is a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1.

a. Patch test
3. Contact dermatitis

b. KOH mount
4. Tinea corporis

c. Biopsy
2. Lupus vulgaris

d. Slit skin smear
1. Leprosy

Lupus vulgaris is one of the prevalent forms of cutaneous tuberculosis that occurs in previously sensitized individuals with high immunity. It is characterized by reddish-brown papules and slow-growing plaques with elevated borders and central atrophy. Diagnosis is made by biopsy. Caseating granulomas are pathognomonic of tuberculosis.

Tinea corporis/ ringworm infection is caused by the dermatophyte Trichophyton rubrum. It results from invasion and proliferation of the causal fungi in the stratum corneum with lesions on the trunk and limbs. Characteristic lesions are circular, usually sharply marginated with a raised edge with central resolution.

KOH mount is used for the diagnosis. Branching hyphae are seen in Tinea corporis.

Leprosy is a chronic granulomatous condition caused by Mycobacterium leprae. It affects the skin, cutaneous and peripheral nerves, and mucous membranes.

Cardinal signs for the diagnosis of leprosy:

• Characteristic skin lesions- hypopigmented or erythematous lesions with definite impairment of sensation.
• Peripheral nerve involvement- thickening of the nerve with sensory impairment. Nerve tenderness can also be seen.
• Detection of acid-fast bacilli in slit-skin smear, skin biopsy, or positive biopsy PCR.

Allergic contact dermatitis is an eczematous reaction that occurs as an immunological response that occurs due to exposure to a substance towards which the immune system has previously been sensitized.

The patch test is used to detect delayed (type IV) hypersensitivity to antigens that come in contact with the skin, by applying the suspected antigen under occlusive patches to the skin. Patches are removed after 48 hours (or sooner if there is itching and burning).

• 48 hours: Patch removal for initial reading to detect delayed hypersensitivity reaction.
• 72-96 hours: Final reading done for confirmation.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: In which condition is Grey-Turner's sign observed?
questions.explanation: Grey-Turner's sign is a clinical sign characterized by ecchymosis (bluish discoloration or bruising) of the flanks. It is a classic indicator of severe Acute Pancreatitis (Option B), specifically the hemorrhagic variety. This bruising results from blood tracked from the retroperitoneum through the transversalis fascia into the subcutaneous tissue of the abdominal wall. Acute appendicitis (Option A), cholecystitis (Option C), and hepatitis (Option D) involve different inflammatory pathways and do not typically lead to the massive retroperitoneal hemorrhage required to produce this sign . Another related sign is Cullen's sign, which involves bruising around the umbilicus. The presence of Grey-Turner's sign signifies a poor prognosis and a high severity of the disease. Therefore, its identification is critical for the risk stratification of patients with acute abdominal pain. It remains the classic pedagogical clinical finding associated with severe, necrotizing pancreatitis in medical board examinations

questions.text: A bus conductor was diagnosed with varicose veins. On examination, skin eczema and lipodermatosclerosis were noted. According to the CEAP classification system, He would be classified as
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. C4

According to CEAP classification, varicose veins with skin eczema and lipodermatosclerosis come under the clinical class of C4.

The clinical class of C4 under CEAP includes changes in skin and subcutaneous tissue secondary to chronic venous disease. It is further classified as,

• C4a- pigmentation or eczema
• C4b- lipodermatosclerosis or atrophie blanche
• C4c- corona phlebectatica

Recent 2020 update on the CEAP system:

• C2r for recurrent varicose veins
• C4c for Corona phlebectatica
• C6r for recurrent active venous ulcer.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient presents with chronic sinusitis, nasal crusting, and a saddle nose deformity. Based on these findings, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis

Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA, formerly Wegener granulomatosis) is an ANCA-associated necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis that classically involves the upper respiratory tract, lungs, and kidneys. Chronic sinusitis, persistent nasal crusting, recurrent epistaxis, and saddle nose deformity due to destruction of the nasal septum are characteristic ENT manifestations and should strongly suggest the diagnosis.

Why not the other options?

• B. Allergic rhinitis: Causes sneezing, rhinorrhea, nasal itching, and pale boggy mucosa; does not cause septal destruction or saddle nose deformity.
• C. Nasal polyposis: Presents with nasal obstruction, hyposmia, and multiple pale polyps; crusting and saddle nose are not typical features.
• D. Rhinoscleroma: A chronic Klebsiella rhinoscleromatis infection causing granulomatous nodules and nasal obstruction, but saddle nose deformity is not a classic presentation.
questions.learning: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA, formerly Wegener granulomatosis) is an ANCA-associated necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis that classically involves the upper respiratory tract, lungs, and kidneys.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 25-year-old woman, gravida 2 with one living child, presents at 18 weeks of gestation with vaginal bleeding for the past 4 hours. On examination, the membranes are ruptured and uterine contractions are present. Transvaginal ultrasonography reveals a cervical length of less than 25 mm with funneling of the internal os measuring more than 1 cm. Based on these findings, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Cervical incompetence (or cervical insufficiency) is the inability of the cervix to retain a pregnancy in the absence of signs and symptoms of clinical contractions, or in response to minimal pressure. However, it often leads to the presentation described: painless dilatation, funneling, and eventually premature rupture of membranes and contractions in the second trimester (16–24 weeks). The ultrasound findings of a short cervix (<25 mm) and "funneling" are highly characteristic markers of an incompetent cervix. Placenta previa (Option B) involves the placenta covering the os and typically presents with "painless" bleeding without ruptured membranes at 18 weeks. Abruptio placentae (Option C) involves premature separation of the placenta and usually presents with "painful" bleeding and a tense uterus later in pregnancy. Traumatic injury (Option D) requires a specific history of trauma. Management for cervical incompetence includes elective cerclage in subsequent pregnancies or emergency cerclage if detected before membranes rupture, though prognosis is poor once rupture has occurred
questions.learning: Cervical incompetence (or cervical insufficiency) is the inability of the cervix to retain a pregnancy in the absence of signs and symptoms of clinical contractions, or in response to minimal pressure.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: A 45-year-old man presents to dermatology with an itchy rash. Examination reveals flat- topped, polygonal, purplish papules with fine white lines, predominantly on the inner wrists, forearms, and lower back. He also reports oral discomfort and white, lacy patches inside his cheeks. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The provided clinical description is pathognomonic for Lichen Planus (Option C) . Lichen planus is defined by the "6 Ps": Purple, Pruritic (itchy), Polygonal, Planar (flat-topped), Papules, and Plaques. The "fine white lines" on the surface are known as Wickham striae. Its characteristic distribution on flexor surfaces like the inner wrists and forearms is typical. Furthermore, the presence of white, lacy patches in the mouth (buccal mucosa) confirms oral lichen planus. Psoriasis (Option A) presents with thick plaques and silvery scales on extensor surfaces (elbows/knees). Eczema (Option B) involves poorly defined, itchy, red patches. Tinea corporis (Option D) is a fungal infection characterized by ring-shaped (annular) lesions with central clearing. Because the patient’s symptoms perfectly match the color, shape, and systemic distribution (oral/cutaneous) of the 6 Ps, Lichen Planus is the definitive diagnosis. It is often associated with Hepatitis C infection
questions.learning: The provided clinical description is pathognomonic for Lichen Planus (Option C) . Lichen planus is defined by the "6 Ps": Purple, Pruritic (itchy), Polygonal, Planar (flat-topped), Papules, and Plaques.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: Crisaborole is a topical agent used for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis. It acts by inhibiting which of the following enzymes?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Phosphodiesterase-4

Crisaborole is a topical phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor used for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis. By inhibiting PDE-4, it increases intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) levels, which reduces the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF-α, IL-2, IL-12), thereby decreasing inflammation and pruritus in eczematous skin.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text: A female singer presents with difficulty producing high-pitched sounds following thyroid surgery. There is no hoarseness in her voice, but she is unable to elevate her pitch. Which nerve is most likely injured?
options: Internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (IBSLN)
External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (EBSLN)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (EBSLN)

The nerve most likely injured in the given case is the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (EBSLN).

The affected muscle is likely the cricothyroid muscle, one of the paired intrinsic muscles of the larynx, which is responsible for elongating and tensing the vocal cords to produce higher pitches. This muscle's function is directly influenced by the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve, which supplies it and facilitates the adjustment of pitch.

The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve descends along the larynx, situated beneath the sternothyroid muscle, to innervate the cricothyroid muscle. By activating this muscle, the external branch enables the tension of the vocal cords to be increased, thereby contributing to the production of higher-pitched sounds. This intricate nerve-muscle interaction highlights the specialised role of the cricothyroid muscle in pitch modulation and vocal quality.

Other options:

Option A: The internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve supplies the mucous membrane of the larynx up to the level of the vocal folds and no motor supply.

Option B: Injury to the right recurrent laryngeal nerve results in hoarseness and dysphonia due to paralysis of the right vocal cord, whereas paralysis of both vocal cords results in aphonia and inspiratory stridor. It supplies all intrinsic muscles of the larynx, except the cricothyroid.

Option C: Lesions of the glossopharyngeal nerve result in the loss of the gag reflex and other sensory loss like taste sensation and loss of pain on tongue, tonsil, pharynx and soft palate. It is motor to the stylopharyngeus, secretomotor to parotid glands, and gustatory to the posterior one-third of the tongue.

questions.topic: Cardiovascular System · All Qbank Qs Excluding Pyqs
questions.text: A 67-year-old man presents with progressive shortness of breath and chest tightness. He has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and long-term smoking. During blood pressure measurement, the cuff is inflated and slowly deflated. At a certain pressure, Korotkoff sounds are heard only during expiration, whereas at a lower pressure, they are heard throughout the respiratory cycle. Which of the following conditions is most likely associated with this physical examination finding?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Pericardial disease

This finding describes pulsus paradoxus, defined as:

• Exaggerated (>10 mm Hg) decrease in systolic blood pressure during inspiration
• Detected by Korotkoff sounds appearing only during expiration at higher pressures

Mechanism:

• Inspiration → ↑ venous return to right heart
• In conditions like cardiac tamponade, the rigid pericardium limits expansion → septum shifts → ↓ LV filling → ↓ systolic BP

Why not other options?

A. Aortic stenosis → Crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur

B. Mitral valve disease → Diastolic murmur or regurgitant murmur

C. Myocardial ischemia → ECG changes, not pulsus paradoxus

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: A 38-year-old man presents to a Suraksha clinic with complaints of anorectal discharge. Under the syndromic management approach for sexually transmitted infections, which color- coded treatment kit is recommended for this condition?
questions.explanation: Under India's Syndromic Case Management (SCM) approach for STIs, color-coded treatment kits are used for standardized management. The Grey kit is specifically recommended for anorectal discharge syndrome. The Grey kit contains medications targeting the common causative organisms of anorectal infections including Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. Why other options are wrong: (B) Green kit is incorrect because the Green kit is used for vaginal discharge syndrome in women, targeting common vaginal infections including bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis, and cervicitis. (C) White kit is incorrect because the White kit is designated for genital ulcer disease syndrome, targeting conditions like syphilis, chancroid, and herpes genitalis causing ulcerative lesions. (D) Blue kit is incorrect because the Blue kit is used for urethral discharge syndrome in males, targeting gonorrhea and chlamydial urethritis — distinct from anorectal discharge which requires the Grey kit
questions.learning: Under India's Syndromic Case Management (SCM) approach for STIs, color-coded treatment kits are used for standardized management. The Grey kit is specifically recommended for anorectal discharge syndrome.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about hair cells?

1. There is 1 row of inner hair cells and 3 rows of outer hair cells
2. Inner hair cells are responsible for transmitting auditory impulses
3. Majority of the afferent fibres of spiral ganglion supply the inner hair cells.
4. Outer hair cells primarily initiate the electrical signals sent to the brain in response to sound vibrations.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. i, ii, iii

Statements i, ii, and iii are correct.

Statement i: There is 1 row of inner hair cells and 3 rows of outer hair cells is a correct statement.

Statement ii: Inner hair cells are responsible for transmitting auditory impulses is a correct statement. Inner hair cells are richly supplied by afferent cochlear fibres and are probably more important in the transmission of auditory impulses.

Statement iii: The majority of the afferent fibres of spiral ganglion supply the inner hair cells is a correct statement. Ninety-five percent of afferent fibres of spiral ganglion supply the inner hair cells while only five percent supply the outer hair cells. Efferent fibres to the hair cells come from the olivocochlear bundle.

Statement iv: Outer hair cells are important in the modulation of basilar membrane action is an incorrect statement. Outer hair cells mainly receive efferent innervation from the olivary complex and are concerned with modulating the function of inner hair cells.
questions.learning: i, ii, iii Statements i, ii, and iii are correct. Statement i: There is 1 row of inner hair cells and 3 rows of outer hair cells is a correct statement.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.text: During rounds, your senior was discussing the given image. The following is an image of which of the following investigations?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. CT scan

The image in the question is a CT scan as it shows the bone as a high-intensity structure (white appearance).

In CT study X-rays are applied in a circular motion and body tissue slices are recreated mathematically. Different tissues are seen with different intensities depending on the proportion of attenuation of the X-rays that pass through them.

• Air and water are displayed as low intensities (dark appearance) because they produce only little attenuation.
• Bone is displayed as a high-intensity structure (bright appearance) because of its significant attenuation.
• High density is seen with hyperemia, freshly clotted blood, and when contrast is used.
• Edema and necrosis are seen as low-intensity lesions.

Other options:

Contrast dye study: In this imaging study, a special dye or contrast is given to evaluate structures that are not identified by conventional imaging. The contrast added would be visible in the image depending on the type of contrast and tissues targeted. Intravenous pyelogram, barium studies, angiography, etc are all examples of contrast studies.

X-ray: It shows different parts of the body in varying shades of black and white. The difference in the appearance of various tissues is due to the differences in the amount of radiation absorbed by them.

• Bone appears white because calcium has high x-ray absorption.
• Fat and soft tissues appear grey due to less x-ray absorption.
• The least absorption is seen with air which appears black.

Angiography: Here a special dye or contrast is injected to highlight the blood vessels are they are not clearly identified in normal imaging. Hence vessels would be highlighted in an angiogram.

Note: A contrast study is different from a contrast-enhanced CT scan, Intravenous pyelogram, barium studies, angiography, etc are all examples of contrast studies.
questions.learning: CT scan — The image in the question is a CT scan as it shows the bone as a high-intensity structure (white appearance). In CT study X-rays are applied in a circular motion and body tissue slices are recreated mathematically.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which area is most frequently affected by head and neck cancer in India?
questions.explanation: In India, the oral cavity is the most frequent site for head and neck cancers. This epidemiological pattern is distinct from many Western countries and is primarily driven by the widespread prevalence of betel quid chewing, areca nut use, and tobacco consumption in various forms like gutka or khaini. These substances are often held in the buccal vestibule for long periods, leading to chronic irritation and malignant transformation of the oral mucosa. Option A (Nasopharynx) is more common in Southeast Asia and linked to EBV. Option B (Oropharynx) is seeing a global rise due to HPV, but tobacco-related oral cavity cancer still predominates in India. Option D (Hypopharynx) is also common among smokers but occurs less frequently than oral cavity lesions. Most Indian patients present with squamous cell carcinoma. Prevention focuses on public health campaigns against "blood-red" spitting and areca nut habits, which are deeply culturally ingrained in many regions

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following statements about Lafutidine is incorrect? 1. Increases gastric mucosal blood flow 2. Acts as an H₂ receptor antagonist 3. Decreases nitric oxide production 4. Increases somatostatin secretion+
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 3 only

Lafutidine is a second-generation H₂ receptor antagonist used for:

• Peptic ulcer disease
• GERD
• Gastritis
• Stress ulcer prophylaxis

What makes it special is that it has both acid-suppressing and mucosal-protective actions.

Correct answer is C because lafutidine is an H₂ receptor antagonist that enhances mucosal defense by increasing gastric mucosal blood flow and stimulating protective mediators. It is known to promote nitric oxide–mediated mucosal protection rather than decrease nitric oxide production. Protective effects include:

| Effect | Mechanism

| ------ | ---------

| ↑ Gastric mucosal blood flow | via nitric oxide

| ↑ Prostaglandin synthesis | mucosal protection

| ↑ Somatostatin secretion | inhibits gastrin

| ↑ Mucus secretion | barrier protection

Thus it protects gastric mucosa beyond acid suppression.
questions.learning: 3 only Lafutidine is a second-generation H₂ receptor antagonist used for: • Peptic ulcer disease • GERD • Gastritis • Stress ulcer prophylaxis What makes it special is that it has both acid-suppressing and mucosal-protective actions.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.text: The graph shown below is the titration curve of a biochemical compound. Which of the following statement is true?
options: The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B
The points A and B represent the range of maximum ionization of the amine and carboxyl group
The compound has three ionisable side chains
The compound has one ionisable group
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B

The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B, which corresponds to the pK1 and pK2 of the compound.

Other options:

• The points A and B represent the pKa of carboxyl and amino groups respectively.
• The amino acid has no ionizable side chains as the graph shows only two pKas.
• The amino acid has two ionizable groups: an amino group and a carboxyl group.

The above graph resembles the titration curve of the amino acid glycine.

Titration curve of Glycine:

The titration is completed at a pH of 12, where the glycine predominantly exists in the form of H2N - CH2 - COO-.

pK1 and pK2 correspond to the point where the buffering capacity is maximum.

Characteristics of the titration curve:

• Buffering capacity is referred to as the ability of the aminoacid to resist the change in pH due to the addition of acid (H+) or base (OH- equivalents), by accepting or losing the protons respectively.
• An ionizable group refers to the group which can either lose or accept a proton and becomes negatively charged or positively charged ion respectively.
• During the titration, the buffering capacity of the compound reaches its maximum, at points where the pKa of the ionizable groups is reached.
• Each of these pKa are labeled as pK1, pK2, pK3, etc.
• The presence of two pKas indicates that the compound has two ionizable groups. Ex. Glycine.
• The presence of three or more pKas indicates the presence of side chains on the amino acid, with additional ionizable groups.
• Ex. histidine has three ionizable groups, an amino group, an imidazole group (on the side chain), and a carboxyl group. The pKas of these groups respectively correspond to the pK1, pK2, pK3 of the titration curve of histidine.
questions.learning: The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B The maximum buffering capacity of the compound is represented by points A and B, which corresponds to the pK1 and pK2 of the compound.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 64-year-old man is rushed to the emergency department with severe abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and obstipation. His erect X-ray abdomen is as shown. Which of the following is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sigmoid volvulus

The given clinical scenario of a 64-year-old man with severe abdominal pain, abdominal distension, and obstipation along with the radiograph showing the coffee bean sign is likely to be sigmoid volvulus.

Sigmoid volvulus is a condition that occurs when the sigmoid colon twists on the sigmoid mesocolon.

A sigmoid volvulus can be differentiated from a cecal volvulus by swirl sign, location of the obstructed loop, and anatomical appendages. The swirl with sigmoid volvulus is located on the right quadrant while the swirl with cecal volvulus is located at the pelvic brim.

Other options:

Option B: Colonic diverticulosis refers to the condition where multiple outpouchings occur along the gastrointestinal tract without any inflammation. The barium enema given below shows multiple outpouchings in the ascending, transverse, and descending colon resembling a saw-tooth.

Option C: Cecal volvulus is more common in females in the 4th to 5th decade. It is characterized by ischemia.

Option D: Paralytic ileus occurs secondary to neuromuscular failure. This leads to the failure of transmission of peristaltic waves. It mainly occurs following laparotomy. The image given below is an X-ray of a patient with a paralytic ileus.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text:
Consider the following actions under AMTSL. Arrange them in the right order:

1. Uterine massage
2.  Give uterotonic (oxytocin 10 mg)
3.  Exclude the presence of another fetus
4.  Controlled cord traction

AMTSL- Active management of the third stage of labor.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 3,2,4,1

The correct sequence in AMTSL is  3,2,4,1.

AMTSL is recommended by the WHO to prevent postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). Uterotonic administration is the most important component in AMTSL. However, even before a uterotonic is administered, the birth attendant will often place their hand over the uterus to ensure that there is no undiagnosed twin.

The currently recommended components of AMTSL are as follows:

Component
Remarks

1.
Injecting uterotonics within 1 minute of delivery of the baby or immediately after delivery of the anterior shoulder

• Most important step
• Oxytocin 10 IU im/iv infusion is the preferred uterotonic.

(Not recommended by WHO- carboprost)

2
Delayed cord clamping

• Done within 1-3 mins of delivery
• 80 ml of additional blood goes to the fetus
• Prevents fetal anemia

3
Delivery of placenta by controlled cord traction: Modified Brandt Andrews technique

• Done only in settings where skilled birth attendants are available
• The uterus is pushed upwards and backward
• The traction of cord is downwards and forwards

4
Intermittent assessment of uterine tone
Done every 15 mins for 2 hours

Note: Uterine massage or fundal massage is not recommended as an intervention to prevent PPH in women who have already received prophylactic uterotonics such as oxytocin (core component of AMTSL). Hence, it is now an optional component of AMTSL that is done in patients with uterine atony as a part of the management of PPH.
questions.learning: 3,2,4,1 The correct sequence in AMTSL is 3,2,4,1. AMTSL is recommended by the WHO to prevent postpartum hemorrhage (PPH).

questions.topic: Cardiovascular System · Acute Coronary Syndrome Mi
questions.text: A 51-year-old man is brought to the emergency department due to chest tightness that started 30 minutes prior to arrival. He has 2 histories of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Initial ECG Shows ST elevation in leads I and aVL. Cardiac enzymes are elevated. Emergent cardiac catheterization in this patient will most likely show occlusion of which of the following arteries?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Left circumflex artery

ST elevation in leads I and aVL localizes to the high lateral wall of the left ventricle. High-lateral STEMI is most commonly due to occlusion of the left circumflex (LCX) (or a diagonal branch), and among the given options LCX best fits.

A. Distal LAD – Usually causes anterior/apical changes (V3–V6), not isolated I/aVL.

C. Left main coronary artery – Produces widespread ST changes with severe instability, not isolated high-lateral.

D. Right coronary artery – Inferior MI (II, III, aVF) ± RV involvement

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A patient presented with dysuria and increased frequency of micturition. He has a history of recurrent urinary tract infections with Proteus species. The radiographic image is given below. Identify the calculi shown.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Calcium Phosphate

The given clinical scenario and X-ray KUB showing a homogenous huge density with the smooth edge seen in the bladder is suggestive of struvite calculi, which is formed due to the precipitation of calcium, magnesium, and ammonium phosphate.

Struvite stones (triple phosphate stones)  are usually seen in a setting of infection with urease-producing bacteria like Proteus, Pseudomonas, and Staphylococcus. They can grow very large and form a cast of the renal pelvis and calyces resulting in staghorn calculi. Production of urease enzyme by Proteus, which hydrolyses urea to ammonia causes alkalinization of urine. Alkalinization of urine leads to precipitation of organic and inorganic compounds which contributes to the formation of Struvite stones.

Almost 90% of the renal stones are radio-opaque and the remaining 10% are radiolucent. The investigation of choice for renal stones is NCCT.

Struvite stones are usually managed with percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) as it is usually larger in size and associated with Urinary tract infections.

Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) is a non-invasive method that generates shockwaves outside the body, which are focused on the stones. It is the most common method of treating urinary tract stones nowadays. Stones up to approximately 1.5 cm in size are suitable for this form of treatment.

PCNL is indicated in:

• Staghorn calculi - Stone >2 cm
• Multiple stones - >1 cm
• Proximal ureteral stone - >1 cm

Other options:
Option A: Patients with cystinuria (an autosomal recessive disorder) are at risk for Cystine stones. These stones are hexagonal.

Option C: Xanthine stones are seen in inborn errors of metabolism like Lesch Nyhan syndrome and cases of hyperuricemia. It is a radiolucent stone.

Option D: Calcium oxalate stones are seen in conditions causing high urine calcium such as primary hyperparathyroidism and chronic acidemia from distal renal tubular acidosis. Also seen in the condition of high urine oxalate which is seen during a low-calcium diet and in malabsorption syndromes(small bowel disease (eg, Crohn's disease), including a jejunoileal bypass for obesity (bariatric surgery), surgical bowel resection or diversion, or cystic fibrosis). Calcium oxalate monohydrate stones are usually dumbbell-shaped and Calcium oxalate dihydrate stones are usually envelope-shaped.
questions.learning: Calcium Phosphate — The given clinical scenario and X-ray KUB showing a homogenous huge density with the smooth edge seen in the bladder is suggestive of struvite calculi, which is formed due to the precipitation of calcium, magnesium, and ammonium phosphate.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: What is the most common presentation of inhalational anthrax?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Hemorrhagic mediastinitis

The most common presentation of inhalation anthrax is hemorrhagic mediastinitis, which is seen in 38% of the patients.

Inhalational anthrax also known as wool sorter’s disease is caused by Bacillus anthracis. Infection usually occurs among workers handling contaminated animal wool, hair, and skin in textile and tanning industries.

Patients present with malaise, fever, cough, shortness of breath & headache. B. anthracis spores are phagocytosed by alveolar macrophages and transported to mediastinal lymph nodes. Hemorrhagic necrosis of the thoracic lymph nodes draining the lung results in hemorrhagic mediastinitis. Pulmonary infiltrates, mediastinal widening, and pleural effusion are other findings.

Treatment of inhalation anthrax includes a combination of intravenous ciprofloxacin and clindamycin for at least 14 days, antitoxins (Raxibacumab, Obiltoxaximab), anthrax immunoglobulins and steroids (if associated meningitis is present).

Prophylaxis with ciprofloxacin (500mg twice daily for 2 months) is recommended for anyone at high risk of inhalational exposure to anthrax spores.
questions.learning: Hemorrhagic mediastinitis — The most common presentation of inhalation anthrax is hemorrhagic mediastinitis, which is seen in 38% of the patients. Inhalational anthrax also known as wool sorter’s disease is caused by Bacillus anthracis.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of a Primary Health Centre?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Physiotherapist

A Primary Health Centre (PHC) is the first point of contact between the community and a medical officer in the public health system. As per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS), the core PHC staff include a Medical Officer, Pharmacist, and Laboratory Technician. A Physiotherapist is not a routine member of the PHC team.

A Physiotherapist is generally posted at higher-level health facilities such as Community Health Centres (CHCs), Sub-District Hospitals, or District Hospitals, not at a standard PHC.

Why not the other options?

• A. Pharmacist: Essential PHC staff responsible for dispensing medicines.
• B. Laboratory Technician: Performs basic laboratory investigations at the PHC.
• C. Medical Officer: In-charge of the PHC and provides clinical and public health services.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.text: A chronic alcoholic is brought to the emergency department with confusion, ataxia, and painful eye movements. The 6th cranial nerve is also involved. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Wernicke's encephalopathy

The above clinical history is suggestive of Wernicke's encephalopathy caused by thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.

Wernicke’s encephalopathy is an acute, neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by nystagmus and ophthalmoplegia, mental status changes (confusion), and unsteadiness of stance and gait (ataxia). It is a medical emergency, and thiamine should be initiated immediately, either intravenously or intramuscularly. The current standard of treatment for patients with symptoms of Wernicke's encephalopathy is to give thiamine 100 mg intravenously before administering glucose-containing IV fluids.

Other options:

Option B: Korsakoff psychosis - While Korsakoff psychosis is also associated with thiamine deficiency and can occur along with Wernicke's encephalopathy, it is primarily characterized by memory loss and confabulation. The presence of confusion, ataxia, and painful eye movements with 6th cranial nerve involvement is more indicative of Wernicke's encephalopathy.

Option C: Delirium tremens - It is a severe form of alcohol withdrawal syndrome and usually occurs within 3-4 days of alcohol withdrawal. The features of delirium tremens are clouding of consciousness, disorientation to time and place, poor attention and distractibility, visual hallucinations and illusions, tachycardia, fever, hypertension, diaphoresis, and pupillary dilatation, and psychomotor agitation and ataxia.

Option D: De Clerembault syndrome (erotomania) - It is characterized by the delusional belief that someone is deeply in love with them. It is more common in women than in men, commonly a young woman who believes that a man whom she considers to be of higher social and/or professional class, is in love with her. This condition is not related to alcohol abuse and does not cause the neurological symptoms described in the question.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: What is the name of the physical sign shown in the image as observed in a 30-year-old male patient?
questions.explanation: The clinical image demonstrates a significant thickening of the distal parts of the fingers and increased curvature of the nail plates, leading to the loss of the normal angle between the nail and the nail bed (Schamroth's window). This finding is known as digital clubbing. It is associated with various chronic conditions including cyanotic heart disease, lung abscesses, bronchiectasis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Spoon-shaped nails (Option A), or koilonychia, are concave and typically associated with chronic iron deficiency anemia. Raynaud's phenomenon (Option B) involves sequential color changes (white to blue to red) in the digits due to vasospasm in response to cold or stress. Pallor (Option C) refers to an abnormal paleness of the skin or mucous membranes often seen in the conjunctiva or nail beds in anemic states. The "drumstick" appearance shown is specifically characteristic of clubbing. Evaluation should focus on identifying the underlying systemic disease responsible for the periosteal changes and increased vascularity in the fingertips

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.text: This is the graph depicting the filterability of dextran through the kidney, 1 representing complete filtration and 0 representing no filtration. Choose the substance A, B, C respectively.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Polycationic, Neutral, Polyanionic

In the given graph, the order of filterability is A>B>C, which likely indicates that the substances are Polycationic, Neutral, Polyanionic.

The glomerular filtration barrier is negatively charged, which will repel most of the negative charged (anionic substances). Whereas, the cationic substances are easily filtered.

Hence, the order of filterability would be: Polycationic > Neutral > Polyanionic, represented by A, B, and C in the graph shown.

The glomerular filtration barrier consists of:

• Endothelium of the capillary
• Basement membrane:

• Lamina densa - electron-dense layer. It contains type IV collagen
• Lamina rara interna - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge
• Lamina rara externa - contains glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate which has a negative charge

• Layer of epithelial cells (podocytes) surrounding the outer surface of the capillary basement membrane

The capillary endothelium is perforated by thousands of small holes called fenestrae, which measure from 4 nm up to 8nm. Therefore, neutral substances with molecular diameters of less than 4 nm are freely filtered, and filtration of those with diameters of more than 8 nm approaches zero.

However, in addition to the size of the particles, the filtration also depends mainly on the charge of the particle being filtered. The glomerular capillary wall consists of highly negatively charged proteins called sialoproteins, which repel the negatively charged substances (anions). The property can be studied by using charged dextran.

When the filtration of the negatively and positively charged dextrans was studied, the results indicated that the negatively charged dextrans in the blood are repelled, with the result that filtration of anionic substances 4 nm in diameter is less than half that of neutral substances of the same size.

This explains, why albumin despite having an effective molecular diameter of approximately 7 nm, has a very low filtration rate.

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.text: A 28-year old pregnant woman came for a routine antenatal check-up in her second trimester. Four years back, she delivered 2 healthy full-term twins. What would her obstetric score be?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. G2P1

The obstetric score of a pregnant woman who previously delivered twins would be G2P1 (gravida 2 para 1).

The term gravida refers to the number of times the woman has been pregnant, irrespective of whether it crossed the period of viability. The current pregnancy is included in this count. Since she has been pregnant once before with twins and is currently pregnant now, gravida will be 2.

The term para refers to the number of previous pregnancies reaching a period of viability (gestation of 28 weeks). It does not increase to a higher number if multiples (twins/triplets) are delivered in a given pregnancy and still count as one birth. A current pregnancy, if any, is not included in this count. Therefore, para here will be 1 since she had one birth of twins and the present pregnancy is not counted.

Both gravidity and parity refer to the pregnancies and not the fetuses.

Note: The period of viability is when the fetus is capable of independent existence. The WHO defines it to be 24 weeks while the Indian definition is 28 weeks.
questions.learning: G2P1 — The obstetric score of a pregnant woman who previously delivered twins would be G2P1 (gravida 2 para 1). The term gravida refers to the number of times the woman has been pregnant, irrespective of whether it crossed the period of viability.
